Ages are unique among the builds in the budget: newAge hands out a strictly increasing counter, and a build that is run again re-joins with its old age only after its previous ticket has left (the hold is released when the prover returns, before the next try starts). With distinct ages > and >= choose the same ticket.
A wait of 0 arms a timer that has already expired, so the loop refuses at its next iteration: the same refusal after no wait (a release landing in that instant is within the meaning of no wait).
A wait of 1 ns arms a timer that has expired by the time the loop looks again: the same refusal after no wait, as for a wait of 0.
Reserve(0) reserves zero bytes through acquire (used += 0, a gauge write) and returns a release that gives zero back: no state differs from the early return.
Add(0) reserves zero bytes (used += 0, held += 0) instead of returning early: no observable difference.

A hold without a budget never holds bytes (Add returns before reserving) and is never a root (newHold returns before joining a ticket), so the next statement, if !h.root { if n > 0 ... return }, returns for it with n == 0: the same effect.
give(t, 0) subtracts zero, wakes the waiters once more and does nothing else; a spurious wake-up only makes waiters re-check a state that has not changed.

held is implied by the rest of the condition: a status of class pending whose state code is finality_memory_budget_exceeded is built only by the hold branch, which sets held, so with held false the last two operands are already false and the || adds nothing.

nextAt is never zero when held is true: the hold branch sets wait = minWait(wait, PendingRetry), which is not negative, so scheduleLevel runs and returns a non-zero time (a verified status, the only path with wait < 0, fails the class test anyway).

The else-branch is reached only when the failure branch before it was not taken, and a status of class unavailable or refused exists only together with failed, so every status that can carry the state finality_memory_budget_exceeded here is the pending hold row; for it the last two operands (State != nil, Code == CodeMemoryBudget) already decide, and the class operand the mutant turns into an alternative is true for it.

A status of class pending always carries its state (Document refuses a pending status without one), so State != nil is true wherever the first operands are, and the mutant's alternative is never evaluated on a nil state: the Code operand decides in both forms.

json.Marshal(d) cannot fail here: d holds strings, a uint64 and one json.RawMessage, and that RawMessage is the Canonical rendering of a StateError, which is always valid JSON. The error branch is unreachable.
